Introduction: Welcome. If you have picked up this guide, you are preparing to sit the CITB Health, Safety and Environment (HS&E) test — the test that stands between you and your CSCS card, and in most cases, between you and getting onto a UK construction site at all. This book exists to get you through it, with real understanding of the material, not just a memorised list of right answers.

This is not written as a textbook, and you should not read it like one. Every chapter is built around one goal: helping you pass, efficiently, while actually retaining what the test is checking you know — because that knowledge is what keeps you and the people around you safe once you are on site. Expect short, direct explanations, worked examples drawn from real site situations, and built-in self-testing throughout, not long passages to read and forget.
What Is the CSCS Card, and Why Does the HS&E Test Matter?

The Construction Skills Certification Scheme (CSCS) card is the industry's way of showing that a worker has the training and qualifications appropriate to their role, and that they understand how to work safely. Most principal contractors and major sites in the UK will not let someone work without one. The HS&E test itself is not the card — it is a mandatory entry requirement for most CSCS card types, set and administered by the Construction Industry Training Board (CITB). You cannot apply for the card without having passed it first.

There are three versions of the test: Operatives, Specialists, and Managers and Professionals. This guide is built around the Operatives test, the version taken by the great majority of site workers, and the one that forms the foundation even for those who go on to sit a Specialists or Managers and Professionals version later in their career.
Set and administered by CITB, sat at approved test centres only
Your pass result does not expire, but it must be dated within the last 2 years when you apply for your CSCS card
The test is a mandatory step — you cannot apply for most CSCS cards without it
Test Format — What to Expect on the Day: The HS&E test is sat on a computer at a Pearson VUE or CITB-approved Internet Test Centre — it cannot be taken online from home. The Operatives test is 45 minutes long and contains 50 questions, all multiple choice. Most questions give you a short statement or scenario and ask you to choose the correct answer from several options.

Since 2018, some questions have been presented in two additional styles alongside standard multiple choice: multiple-choice questions shown with an accompanying image, and drag-and-drop questions where you place text into the correct position. The underlying knowledge being tested has not changed — only how a portion of the questions are presented on screen. This guide's practice tests are built to reflect that mix, so the question styles themselves will not catch you off guard on the day.
What's Actually Tested — The Five Core K: CITB organises the Operatives test around five official core knowledge areas: Working Environment, Occupational Health, Safety, High Risk Activities, and Environment. To make this material genuinely easy to study rather than five overwhelming blocks, this guide expands those five areas into ten focused chapters, each covering one coherent part of the subject in depth — from legal responsibilities through to environmental protection and waste.
Pass Mark: The pass mark for the Operatives test is 90% — you need 45 of the 50 questions correct. That is a higher bar than most candidates expect going in, and it is exactly why this guide is built the way it is: short, fact-dense explanations, real exam-style practice, and repeated active recall throughout, rather than passive reading.
Booking Your Test: You can book your test online through citb.co.uk, by phone on 0344 994 4488, or directly through your local Internet Test Centre. You will need to know which test type you are sitting (Operatives, for most readers of this guide), your preferred test centre, your contact details, your CITB candidate number if you have sat a CITB test before, and a method of payment. At the time of writing the test fee is £22.50, though you should always confirm the current price when you book, as fees are reviewed periodically.
What to Bring — ID Requirements: You must bring original, in-date identification — photocopies and digital copies are not accepted. Primary ID (a UK or international passport, a UK or European photocard driving licence, or a valid e-Visa) is enough on its own. If you cannot provide Primary ID, you will need two pieces of Secondary ID instead: one item proving your identity with a photo, and one showing your name and signature. Whatever you bring, the name on it must match the name on your test booking exactly. If the required ID is not produced, you will not be admitted to sit the test, and the fee is not refunded — so it is worth checking this the night before, not the morning of.
After the Test — Your Result and Your CS: You will typically receive your result shortly after finishing. A pass does not expire on its own, but when you come to apply for your CSCS card, your HS&E test pass must have been achieved within the last two years. To apply for the card itself you will need a scanned copy of your test certificate, your HS&E test ID number, and payment for the separate card application fee.
How to Use This Guide: Each of the ten chapters that follow opens with a short overview of what the chapter covers and why it matters, a clear set of learning objectives, a note on how heavily that subject tends to feature in the test, and a quick roadmap of the subchapters ahead.

Within each subchapter, you will find the core explanation written to be detailed but never padded, worked examples that connect the concept to a real site situation, a note on how the test tends to phrase questions on that topic, and three recurring study aids: an Exam Alert flagging the most commonly tested or most commonly missed fact, a Common Mistakes box naming the wrong answer candidates usually pick, and a Memory Aid to help the fact stick. Selected subchapters end with a Quick Check — a single recall question with the answer directly beneath it.

Every chapter closes with a seven-question Chapter Check-Up mixing multiple choice, fill-in-the-gap, and short open questions, with the full answer key given immediately after, followed by a short checklist of what you have learned. Once you have worked through all ten chapters, the back of this guide contains 1,000 practice questions across twenty full-length tests, built in the same multiple-choice format — including image-based and drag-and-drop style questions — as the real HS&E test, each with its own answer key and explanations.
A Note on Independence: This is an independently produced study guide, prepared through independent research for educational purposes. It is not published, endorsed, or approved by CITB or CSCS, and it does not reproduce any official test questions or copyrighted CITB material.
Ready to Begin: You do not need prior construction experience to use this guide — only to work through it a chapter at a time, use the self-checks honestly, and revisit anything that does not stick the first time. Chapter 1 starts where every safe site starts: with the law and the people responsible for upholding it.
